candidates.evidence: Measured 165.8 cm-1 (A1g2 reference ~165, Shahil et al. arXiv:1201.5678 Fig. 5, 488 nm, ~40 nm film) and 120.3 cm-1 (Eg2 reference ~115, same figure, +5 cm-1). Mismatches: expected A1g1 ~70 cm-1 vs measured 79.7 (+10 cm-1, too large for a calibration offset), and the strongest measured band at 104.5 cm-1 has no Sb2Te3 counterpart. No Eg1 (~35 cm-1) is in the 60 cm-1 window. Partial match only.

Jiang et al. arXiv:1501.04898 Fig. 2a (bulk, 300 K): A2^4 ~110, A1^9 ~120, A1^8 ~132, A1^6 ~141, A1^5 ~161, A1^2 ~210 cm-1. 120 and 166 cm-1 fall near A1^9 and A1^5. Inconsistent: the strong A1^2 band near 210 cm-1 is absent (only a marginal feature near 218 cm-1), and 80 and 104 cm-1 have no counterpart.

Measured 104.5 cm-1 matches Eg2 (~102-104 cm-1, Shahil et al. arXiv:1201.5678 Fig. 6a, 633 nm). The A1g2 band (~135 cm-1) is absent from the data (the only point near 138 cm-1 is a single-sample feature), and 120 and 166 cm-1 are unexplained. Inconsistent.
Reference Eg2 ~131 and A1g2 ~172-175 cm-1 (Shahil et al. arXiv:1201.5678 Fig. 6b; Kim et al. arXiv:1112.1364 abstract for A1g2 dominance). Neither band is present at those positions. Inconsistent.

candidates.material: Trigonal Te precipitates on or in a telluride
candidates.evidence: Manjon et al. arXiv:2102.11580 report broad anomalous bands at 119-145 cm-1 in many tellurides, attributed to trigonal Te clusters, and link them to laser heating. A band near 120 cm-1 is therefore compatible with Te segregation, but the expected Te E1 (~92 cm-1) and E2 (~140 cm-1) bands are not clearly present, and the paper does not give the Te mode positions. Not confirmed.

Position and FWHM measured (+/-0.34 cm-1; fitted Gaussian fraction 0.6). Matched to Sb2Te3 A1g2 ~165 cm-1 in Shahil et al. arXiv:1201.5678 Fig. 5 (488 nm). Good agreement, but the other bands are unexplained.

citations: arXiv:1201.5678 (Shahil, Hossain, Goyal, Balandin, Micro-Raman of few-quintuple Bi2Te3, Bi2Se3, Sb2Te3): Fig. 5 (Sb2Te3, 488 nm) and Fig. 6 (Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3, 633 nm) used for reference mode positions
arXiv:1501.04898 (Jiang, Gao, Wang, Raman fingerprint of WTe2): Fig. 2a used for WTe2 bulk mode positions
arXiv:2102.11580 (Manjon et al., Anomalous Raman modes in tellurides): broad bands 119-145 cm-1 attributed to trigonal Te; used only for the Te-precipitate alternative
arXiv:1112.1364 (Kim et al., Temperature dependence of Raman-active optical phonons in Bi2Se3 and Sb2Te3): abstract only, A1g2 described as dominant mode
limits: Identity not established. The four strong bands fit no single candidate: Sb2Te3 matches 120 and 166 cm-1 only, and the 80 and 104 cm-1 bands are unexplained. This is a partial match, not an identification.

No DFT library ranking was run. The skill's scripts (rl_qc.py, rl_fit.py, rl.py) live outside this working folder, and I kept to the folder as instructed. The fit, spike check and peak search were done directly with numpy, scipy and lmfit on ./spectrum.csv.

The data is noisy. Point-to-point scatter is about 500 counts, and 276 of 1152 points are exactly 0.0, so the trace looks clipped at zero, probably by background subtraction on export. The fit residual RMS (about 1250 counts over 60-200 cm-1) is above the point noise, so the fitted widths and amplitudes are approximate.
The 79.7 cm-1 band sits about 20 cm-1 above the 60 cm-1 low-frequency cutoff of the data. The notch-filter edge may distort its width and position, so treat it as uncertain.

No Si reference line at 520.7 cm-1 was found, so there is no internal frequency calibration. Absolute positions could be offset by several cm-1. Sampling is 0.9 cm-1 per point and the instrumental resolution is not given, so widths below about 3 cm-1 cannot be trusted.
Weak features at 218, 255, 316, 360, 482 and 508 cm-1 were seen only after heavy smoothing and are close to the noise. They are not reported as peaks.

Reference positions are from the abstracts or figure readings of arXiv:1201.5678 and arXiv:1501.04898 (read from plots, roughly +/-2 cm-1) and from the Manjon abstract. The Sb2Te3 numbers come from a 488 nm, 40 nm film, and the Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3 numbers from 633 nm, while this spectrum was taken at 532 nm. Resonance and thickness effects can shift relative intensities and positions.

Temperature is 295 K, so there is no low-temperature check. The laser at 532 nm is not resonant with the candidates' gap features as far as I checked, so resonance does not explain the missing bands, but this was not verified.

To settle the identity: (1) measure a reference Sb2Te3 and Bi2Te3 film at 532 nm with a Si line for calibration; (2) lower the laser power to test whether the 120 cm-1 band is trigonal Te from laser heating (arXiv:2102.11580); (3) measure a wider spectral range (to about 300 cm-1 with clear high-frequency modes) and at higher resolution; (4) check composition with EDX or XPS.
